blocks.content: Covers key historical, political, and cultural figures associated with Bihar — a heavily biographical area tested through direct name-to-contribution matching, spanning from ancient statecraft to the modern republic.

Bihar's roll of historically significant figures begins, fittingly, with the architects of ancient Indian statecraft — Chandragupta Maurya and his strategist Chanakya, and Ashoka the Great, all covered in depth in this book's history chapters. But Bihar's contribution to Indian public life extends with equal weight into the modern era, beginning with Dr. Rajendra Prasad, born in Zeeradei (in present-day Siwan district), who combined a leading role in the Champaran Satyagraha with subsequent service as President of the Constituent Assembly of India and, upon independence, as independent India's first President (1950–1962) — a tenure of twelve years that remains the longest of any Indian President to date.

Bihar has also produced towering figures in social reform and socialist politics. Jayaprakash Narayan ('JP'), though born in present-day Bihar, became a national figure through his early socialist activism and, decades later, his leadership of the broad-based 'JP Movement' (Sampoorna Kranti, or 'Total Revolution') of the mid-1970s, which mobilized opposition to Indira Gandhi's government and is widely credited with shaping the political landscape that led to the imposition and eventual end of the Emergency (1975–1977). Karpoori Thakur, twice Chief Minister of Bihar and a pioneering figure in implementing reservation policy for backward classes within the state, was posthumously awarded the Bharat Ratna in 2024, a recognition of his enduring influence on Bihar's — and India's — social justice politics.

Bihar's cultural sphere has been similarly influential: Maithili poet Vidyapati (14th–15th century), whose devotional and lyrical compositions in Maithili and Sanskrit profoundly shaped subsequent Indian devotional literature and are still widely sung and studied; and in the modern era, cricketer M. S. Dhoni (born in Ranchi, in present-day Jharkhand, but whose career and public identity remain closely and popularly associated with the broader Bihar/Jharkhand region prior to Jharkhand's 2000 formation), among many other prominent contemporary figures across sport, cinema, and public administration.

items: Chandragupta Maurya and Ashoka the Great — founders and consolidators of the Mauryan Empire, covered in full depth in the Ancient History chapter of this book.

Dr. Rajendra Prasad — born in Zeeradei, Siwan district; key figure in the Champaran Satyagraha; President of the Constituent Assembly of India; first President of independent India (1950–1962), serving the longest tenure of any Indian President.

Karpoori Thakur — twice served as Chief Minister of Bihar; a pioneering leader in implementing reservation policy for socially and economically backward classes within the state; posthumously awarded the Bharat Ratna in 2024.

Jayaprakash Narayan ('JP') — prominent socialist leader whose 'JP Movement' (Sampoorna Kranti) of the mid-1970s mobilized major national political opposition and profoundly shaped Indian politics around the Emergency period; posthumously awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1999.

Anugrah Narayan Sinha — a key associate of Rajendra Prasad in the freedom movement, and Bihar's first Deputy Chief Minister and Finance Minister after independence, remembered for his role in the state's early post-independence development.

Numerous other Bihar-origin leaders contributed to the freedom movement at both the state and national levels, particularly during the Champaran Satyagraha and the subsequent Non-Cooperation, Civil Disobedience, and Quit India movements covered in the History chapter.

Vidyapati (c. 14th–15th century) — celebrated Maithili and Sanskrit poet whose devotional lyric compositions profoundly influenced subsequent Indian devotional literature and continue to be sung and studied, particularly within Mithila's cultural tradition.

Bihar's Madhubani painting tradition (covered in the Culture chapter) has produced numerous celebrated contemporary artists who have helped bring the art form to national and international recognition.

The state's rich oral and folk traditions have similarly produced figures of regional and national renown across music, storytelling, and performance arts, reflecting Bihar's broader cultural depth beyond its most internationally famous exports.

Bihar has produced numerous prominent contemporary figures across politics, administration, sport, and cinema; candidates should stay updated on recent Padma award recipients and other national honours given to Bihar-origin individuals, as these are frequently tested in current-affairs-linked GK sections.

Reviewing recent (last 2–3 years) Padma award lists and other major national recognitions for Bihar-connected individuals is a high-value, low-effort current-affairs preparation step given how consistently this category is tested.

Exam Tip

• Rajendra Prasad's specific distinction (longest-serving Indian President, 1950–1962) is a guaranteed, precisely-worded recurring question.

• Karpoori Thakur's 2024 Bharat Ratna is a recent, high-salience current-affairs fact worth knowing precisely given how recently it was awarded.

• Distinguishing Jayaprakash Narayan's 'JP Movement'/Sampoorna Kranti (1970s) from earlier freedom-movement-era figures is a commonly tested chronological distinction — JP's major national impact came well after independence, not during the freedom struggle itself.
